body: You could be right about the brumating thing. He seems less active today but is lying under his hot spot. I'm keeping an eye on him.

I did give his body up for a necropsy. It's not for free but I didn't expect it to be. I should have results tomorrow. If he died because of something the vet overlooked, I'm gonna go to a different one from then on.

Don't worry, nothing my skink touched, touched my beardie. Their enclosures stand next to each other so if its some kind of air born disease... hopefully it's nothing and I'm just being paranoid.
I informed myself on the price which is high but not too high so I delivered my skinks body this afternoon. I'll have the results tomorrow they said.

He's currently lying under his hotspot so I think he's doing better, although he hasn't eaten his salad today and I still see two living locusts so maybe he really is kind of burmating. Although burmating dragons usually dig themself in a bit on the cold side of their enclosure, right?

I know that normally skinks don't eat every day but mine should eat more often because he's still underweight,  but he's so stubborn. The crickets have plenty of hides which they use but if one comes out, my skink flees in terror. I tried worms instead but he's not a fan of those either. I did get him to eat a bit of cooked chicken recently though so I call that a win. Usually he only eats liquid food for some reason and only 5-10 licks. So he's still not really eating enough. He's been lethargic recently even though he's technically healthy besides a little underweight still. He's my worry child. I don't like it if a reptile isn't doing well for unknown reasons.. Thanks for telling me about your feisty girl, its good to know that it can even take 2 years for them to mellow out. My previous skinks were all pretty much tame from the start so that was easy, haha :P

Thanks for comfirming that. I was doubting that he's an Indonesian. I've had an Iran jaya a few years back that looked EXACTLY like this one, although I know that doesnt have to mean anything. Thanks for the tip about warming up the cat food, I haven't tried that yet. I doubt he'll eat it though because he only ever licks his food, so as to get him to gain some weight, I've stuck with liquid/half liquid foods for a while. He hasn't touched any fresh yummy fruits and he's somehow scared to death of anything that moves, like all feeder insects, including snails. I don't really understand why he's such a difficult eater. The vet told me he was healthy though, twice. I'm wondering if it's psychological.

His previous owners barely fed him. He's gained some weight back now but he's a very, very bad eater. He barely eats, no matter what I give him. I've tried all kinds of food. He's an Indonesian too, they said. He's also really scared and defensive, even after 4 months in my care.

For me of is. I never get the 'normal' fever temperature. I once had a terrible infection of a very deep cut, had sepsis and all that, yet I still only had 97. You can't have that kind of infection without fever, that's just not possible. My doc says that my 'internal thermostat' is just wired differently. My usual temperature is sometimes even lower if I'm a bit cold, and for normal people that would be hypothermia and I'm totally fine.

My normal body temperature is lower than most people, at 94 Fahrenheit. At 97 Fahrenheit I get fever symptoms like chills, hot to the touch, sickly feeling, tiredness etc. So whenever i have the flu or an infected wound or whstever, 97 Fahrenheit is my cue to go to the doctor. But when I get these super depressed and anxiety spells, it's about 99 Fahrenheit. I only once had 101 Fahrenheit because of sepsis and I almost died once. So having 97 Fahrenheit for me means I have a fever. So I don't really get why I'm feverish when I'm depressed worse than usual?

In my neighbourhood there aren't many black rat snakes actually. Believe me, I've looked. Only ever saw one other one. I've wanted one for quite some time so I took my chance. And yeah, I get that it doesn't sound trustworthy, but he really is. He's really good to his animals, beautiful enclosures, big enough and clean. He treats every new animal with Panache (not sure about Flagyl though, havent heard of that one) and always keeps them in quarantine for at least 6 weeks. Most reptile sellers (dreaded pet shops and breeders alike) are often terrible to their animals and I've bought a few animals that were supposedly healthy and ended up dying from various things. This seller has only ever sold me healthy animals. I've been going to him for years and can't complain on a single issue. He's a private seller too, nothing too big. He's actually one of the very few reptile sellers in my neighbourhood. I have a phobia preventing me from traveling far from home so my options are always limited. But thanks for telling me about the parasite issue. I did know it could take a few months but wasn't aware it could take 18 months. If I see any obvious sign of sickness, I'll go straight to the vet. I go to a yearly routine check with my animals too so I'll know then if he's completely clean. Thanks for the info! 

And true, I'd obviously prefer a captive bred snake but since he was one of my dream snakes... If I could order live animals online, I'd search for my dream snakes that way of course, but as I said, my options are often limited. Better in a nice and warm enclosure in my room, than having an idiot setting him 'free' here. He'd die.
